subject.name: SkinGPT / Janus Shell tactile and thermal sensing subsystem
subject.research_role: bio-derived / low-cost robotic tactile-thermal sensing and recovery research

implemented_system.classifier_status: transparent rule-based baseline; no trained neural classifier claimed

bio_derived_research_direction.goal: Use bacterial-cellulose/SCOBY-derived material as part of a tactile sensing skin for autonomous recovery systems, with piezoelectric and thermal sensing layers.
bio_derived_research_direction.current_boundary: No integrated SCOBY sensing panel has yet been validated in the current repository.
bio_derived_research_direction.scientific_requirement: Material sensing claims require measured panel characterization, humidity/drift controls, repeatable mechanical loading and comparison against non-SCOBY controls.

prior_art_boundary.work: Multifunctional Flexible PVDF-TrFE/BaTiO3 Based Tactile Sensor for Touch and Temperature Monitoring
prior_art_boundary.known_feature: PVDF-TrFE/BaTiO3 flexible touch and temperature sensing
prior_art_boundary.boundary: PVDF/BaTiO3 tactile-temperature sensing is not claimed novel

prior_art_boundary.work: A Scalable Bacterial Cellulose Ionogel for Multisensory Electronic Skin
prior_art_boundary.known_feature: bacterial-cellulose-derived multisensory e-skin responding to pressure, touch, temperature, humidity and other stimuli
prior_art_boundary.boundary: Bacterial-cellulose e-skin is not claimed novel

candidate_delta.focus: Recovery-oriented, auditable sensor subsystem rather than a generic e-skin material demonstration.
candidate_delta.composition: Low-cost bio-derived material direction + segmented tactile/thermal telemetry + health/reboot/gap provenance + calibration workflow + future damage-localization/recovery integration.
candidate_delta.novelty_status: APPLICATION/ARCHITECTURE_CANDIDATE_ONLY; requires dedicated e-skin and robotics prior-art review plus physical material validation

safe_public_claims.short: I developed SkinGPT, an experimental tactile/thermal sensing subsystem for robotic shells and autonomous recovery research, with an ESP32-S3 data path and a bio-derived bacterial-cellulose/SCOBY material direction.
safe_public_claims.technical: The current runnable baseline provides segmented thermal sensing, piezoelectric event capture, calibration, health telemetry and replayable NDJSON data; the integrated SCOBY sensing panel remains an unvalidated research target.

next_scientific_gate: fabricate and characterize an integrated bacterial-cellulose/SCOBY sensing coupon
add 3-4 piezo channels or segmented electrodes for localization
add humidity compensation and material-drift logging
run blinded controlled impact/thermal tests against conventional substrate controls
publish calibration data and failure/null results
